by the UK. An adequacy decision is not required when: 
- 
the data subject has unambiguously given his consent (which is applicable to 
opening and operating Hong Kong accounts by natural persons customers of 
London Branch); 
- 
the transfer is necessary for the performance of a contract between the data 
subject and the data controller; 
- 
the transfer is necessary to implement pre-contractual measures taken in 
response to the subject’s request; 
- 
the transfer is necessary for the conclusion or performance of a contract 
concluded in the interest of a data subject between the data controller and a 
third party (which is applicable to keep backups of London Branch’s personal 
data in Hong Kong); 
- 
the transfer is necessary to protect the vital interest of the data subject, where 
the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; or 
- 
the transfer is taken to be necessary for reasons of substantial public interest. 
8A.3 In the absence of an adequacy decision and the exceptions set out in paragraph 8A.2, 
the UKGDPR introduces the possibility of transfers being made on the basis of 
appropriate safeguards, including but not limited to an approved code of conduct, 
certification mechanism or a legal instrument containing standard contractual 
clauses adopted by the UK, and binding and enforceable commitments (such as 
binding corporate rules) of the data controller or the data processor that is outside 
the UK. In this regard, in relation to data transfers between the Bank and its 
overseas branches, the Bank has in place an intra-group transfer agreement that 
incorporates the standard contractual clauses adopted by the UK.  
8A.4 For international data transfers in other circumstances, please refer to Appendix 10. 
=== PAGE 30 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 30 / 76 
8B. PIPL: Cross-border transfers of personal data1  
Personal data should not be transferred out of the Mainland, unless separate consents 
from the data subjects have been obtained, and where applicable, the necessary 
certification by professional institutions, Standard Contract Provisions (see Appendix 17 
for the template as formulated by the CAC) with the overseas recipient, registration with 
or approval by the CAC, has been obtained, signed or sought in accordance with the 
assessment criteria as illustrated in Appendix 18. 
9. Outsourcing 
9.1. In the case of outsourcing work to Service Provider, extra care should be taken 
where the Service Provider is entrusted to handle the personal data in the course of 
performing services. 
9.2. If personal data are accessible by the Service Provider, it is essential to take 
measures to prohibit the Service Provider from conveying the data to third parties 
(i.e. prohibition clause shall be included in the service contract with the Service 
Provider). 
9.3. The Bank should notify the customers in general terms of the possibility that their 
data may be transferred to Service Provider by means of the Personal Data Circular. 
The Bank should also give specific notice to customers of significant outsourcing 
initiatives, especially when the outsourcing is to an overseas jurisdiction. 
9.4. For the purposes under this paragraph, any department initiating an outsourcing 
proposal should follow the Bank’s Guidelines on Outsourcing and Insourcing under 
which a detailed risk assessment covering the area of customer data protection is 
included and adequate control procedures should be established to ensure related 
risk is mitigated. 
10. UKGDPR: Service Provider Processing Agreement 
10.1. When engaging Service Providers as data processors, the engagement contract 
1 According to the CAC, cross-border remittance is not considered as involving cross-border transfer of personal 
data. 
=== PAGE 31 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 31 / 76 
shall stipulate, in particular, that the Service Providers: 
10.1.1. processes the personal data only on the Bank’s documented instructions; 
10.1.2. seeks the Bank’s authorization to transfer personal data to a third country 
or an international organisation (unless required to do so by a law to which 
the processor is subject); 
10.1.3. shall inform the Bank of any such legal requirement to transfer data before 
processing; 
10.1.4. ensures that persons authorised to process the personal data have 
committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate 
statutory obligation of confidentiality; 
10.1.5. takes all measures to security the personal data at all times; 
10.1.6. respects, supports and complies with the Bank’s obligation to respond to 
requests for exercising the data subject's rights; 
10.1.7. assists the Bank in ensuring compliance with the Bank’s obligations for 
data security, mitigating risks, breach notification and privacy impact 
assessments; 
10.1.8. when requested, deletes or returns all personal data to the Bank after the 
end of the provision of services relating to processing, and deletes existing 
copies where possible;  
10.1.9. makes available to the Bank, all information necessary to demonstrate 
compliance with the obligations set out here and in the contract; 
10.1.10. allows and supports audits, monitoring, inspections and reporting as set 
out in the contract; and 
10.1.11. informs the Bank immediately of any breaches, non-compliance or 
inability to carry out their duties as detailed in the contract. 
10.2. A template “Data Processor Agreement” has been prepared by the Bank for this 
=== PAGE 32 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 32 / 76 
purpose (Appendix 9) for reference only, please consult Legal Department before 
use. 
11. Sharing and Use of Consumer Credit Data through Credit Reference Agencies 
11.1. The Bank may share and use consumer credit data through Credit Reference 
Agencies (“CRAs”) from time to time. Since the consumer credit data involved 
may contain personal data as defined in the Ordinance, the departments involving 
in the sharing or use of personal data through CRAs should act in line with the 
requirements stipulated in (i) the Code of Practice on Consumer Credit Data issued 
by the Privacy Commissioner, (ii) the Supervisory Policy Manual IC-6 “The 
Sharing and Use of Consumer Credit Data through Credit Reference Agencies” 
issued by the HKMA, and (iii) Code of Practice for Multiple Credit Reference 
Agencies Model issued by the Hong Kong Association of Banks. 
11.2. Scope of data to be provided on consumer credit data by credit provider or debt 
collection agencies to CRA  
11.2.1. Scope of data to be provided on consumer credit data by credit provider to 
CRA  
11.2.1.1. 
Where the consumer credit data are not collected in relation to a 
mortgage loan  
A general particulars of the individual, being: name, address, contact 
information, date of birth, Hong Kong Identity Card Number or travel 
document number; 
Credit application data (being the fact that the individual has made an 
application for consumer credit, the type and the amount of credit 
sought) that do not relate to a mortgage loan;  
Account general data, being: identity of the credit provider; account 
number; capacity of the individual (whether as borrower, mortgagor or 
guarantor); account opened date; account closed date; type of the 
facility and currency denominated; approved credit limit or loan 
amount (as appropriate); repayment period or terms (if any); account 
status (active, closed, write-off, etc.); facility maturity date (if any);  
=== PAGE 33 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 33 / 76 
For details of any scheme of arrangement, including: the date of the 
arrangement, the number and frequency of installments, the installment 
amount, etc.; and  
In the case of a hire-purchase, leasing or charge account, including: 
account expiry date, type of security, investigation date, installment 
amount, etc; particulars for the identification of the motor vehicles, 
equipment, vessels or the asset secured by the charge, and notification 
of termination of the charge.  
Account repayment data, being: amount last due; amount of payment 
made during the last reporting period; remaining available credit or 
outstanding balance;  
Default data being: amount past due (if any) and number of days past 
due; date of settlement of amount past due (if any); date of final 
settlement of amount in material default (if any);  
Credit card loss data, being: notice that the credit provider, as card 
issuer, has suffered financial loss as the result of an unauthorized 
transaction carried out through the use of a credit card that has been 
reported lost, for an amount in excess of the maximum liability of the 
individual before notification to the card issuer of the loss of the card; 
the amount of such maximum liability and the amount of financial loss 
suffered by the card issuer; the reported date of the loss of the credit 
card, and the date of such report; and a description of the event 
(misplacement of wallet, theft, robbery, etc.) reported to have given rise 
to the loss of the credit card and any follow-up action including, where 
applicable, any report to the police, subsequent investigation or 
prosecution and result, finding of the lost card, etc. 
Credit provider shall not provide the following data to the CRA: 
Account data of any account which has been terminated by full 
repayment (excluding payment by refinancing of the debit balance on 
the account by the credit provider) prior to 2 June 2003; or  
Account repayment data held by it prior to 2 June 2003 of any account 
=== PAGE 34 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 34 / 76 
which already existed prior to 2 June 2003 and continues to exist after 
that date, unless such account repayment data reveal an outstanding 
default on 2 June 2003, in which case, the credit provider may provide 
to the CRA the default data relating to such default;  
11.2.1.2. 
 Where the consumer credit data is collected in relation to a mortgage 
loan  
Mortgage account general data, being: name of the individual; capacity 
of the individual (i.e. whether as borrower, mortgagor or guarantor); 
Hong Kong Identity Card Number or travel document number; date of 
birth; address; account number; type of the facility; account status 
(active, closed, write-off, etc); account closed date;  
Credit provider shall not provide the following data to the CRA:  
The mortgage account general data of any account relating to a 
mortgage loan which has been terminated by full repayment prior to 1 
April 2011; or 
The mortgage account general data of any account relating to a 
mortgage loan which already existed prior to 1 April 2011 and 
continues to exist after that date unless: 
The credit provider has obtained the prescribed consent of the 
individual to whom the data relates for disclosure of the mortgage 
account general data to the CRA; or 
The repayment data of such account reveals a currently outstanding 
material default, in which case, the credit provider may provide to the 
CRA the account general data together with the default data relating to 
such material default; 
Mortgage application data (being the fact that the individual has made 
an application for mortgage loan) provided that the credit provider has 
obtained the prescribed consent of the individual; and 
Where there is any outstanding material default of a mortgage loan 
=== PAGE 35 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 35 / 76 
which is granted on or after 1 April 2011, the credit provider may 
provide to the CRA the account general data together with the default 
data relating to such material default. 
11.2.2. Scope of data to be provided on consumer credit data by debt collection 
agencies to CRA 
If a credit provider engages a DCA for collection against an individual in 
default, it may provide to the agency only information relating directly to 
the individual consisting of the following: 
11.2.2.1. 
Particulars to enable identification and location of the individual, 
including address and contact information;  
11.2.2.2. 
The nature of the credit;  
11.2.2.3. 
Amount to be recovered and details of any goods subject to 
repossession.  
Note: The information under section 11 is compiled from the "Code of Practice 
on Consumer Credit Data” January 2013 Fourth Revised Edition issued by the 
Privacy Commissioner.  
12. Direct Marketing and Cross-Marketing Activities 
12.1. Direct marketing by the Bank 
12.1.1. Direct marketing (e.g. sending marketing / promotional materials by mail,         
facsimile transmission, electronic mail, or making telephone calls, etc. to a 
specific individual) is a common business practice adopted by the Bank to 
promote its business to its existing customers. The process often involves 
the collection and use of personal data and hence compliance with the 
requirements under the Ordinance is essential. 
12.1.2. The Bank shall not, without customer’s written consent, use personal data 
obtained from the customers for direct marketing purpose or provide 
personal data to another person (including group companies of the Bank) 
for use in direct marketing. 
=== PAGE 36 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 36 / 76 
12.1.3. The Bank shall not receive money or other property in return for providing 
personal data to another person for direct marketing. 
12.1.4. The Privacy Commissioner has issued a guidance note, namely New 
Guidance on Direct Marketing (a copy of which can be obtained at 
https://www.pcpd.org.hk//english/resources_centre/publications/files/GN_
DM_e.pdf), to govern the conduct of direct marketing activities. All units 
of the Bank which engage or intend to engage in such activities have to 
observe the requirements stated under the New Guidance on Direct 
Marketing. 
12.1.5. While the Bank may use personal data in conducting direct marketing 
activities, personal data must not be collected from public sources (e.g. a 
telephone directory of a trade union or professional body, online telephone 
directory information of Government officials provided by the Government, 
register of electors, etc.) for direct marketing purpose. 
12.1.6. Section 35F of the Ordinance requires a data user on the first occasion that 
it uses an individual’s personal data for direct marketing to inform the 
individual that he or she may, on a no charge basis, request the data user to 
cease to use his or her personal data. If the data user makes such a request, 
the data user should cease to use the data concerned. This arrangement is 
generally described as “opt-out”. 
12.1.7. For the purpose of fulfilling the requirements under section 35F of the 
Ordinance, when the Bank uses personal data the first time for direct 
marketing activities, the Bank shall give the data subject the “opt-out” 
choice. High-level principles of “opt-out” choice are as follows: 
- 
Where the marketing approach is made by telephone, the telemarketer 
should inform the called party of his right to opt out by making clear 
to him that if he does not wish to have further marketing approach 
from our Bank, he can inform the telemarketer and our Bank will not 
use his personal data for direct marketing purpose. For audit trail 
purpose, the telemarketing call made should be audio-recorded. 
- 
Where the marketing approach is made by other means (e.g. by mail, 
by fax, by email, etc.) the marketing material should state clearly the

{"output": "13. Data Access Requests  
13.1. Customers have a right to ascertain with the Bank whether their personal data is 
held and if the Bank holds such data, to obtain a copy of their personal data (“data 
access request”). 
13.1.1. For minors under the age of 18, a person who has parental responsibility 
for the minor may make a data access request on his or her behalf; for a 
person who is unable to handle his or her own affairs, a person appointed 
by the court to handle such matters may make a data access request on his 
or her behalf. 
13.1.2. The Customer may request the Bank to provide a copy of the information 
in a designated language, but if the Bank does not have the information in 
the designated language, the Bank will only provide a copy of the text in 
original language without translation. 
13.1.3. The Customer may request the Bank to provide a copy of the information 
in specified form, but if it is not practicable, the Bank may provide a copy 
in other forms. 
=== PAGE 51 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 51 / 76 
13.2. The Bank is required to comply with a data access request within 40 days after 
receiving the request. If it is unable to comply with the request, in whole or in part, 
within the 40 day reply period, the Bank must within such period inform the data 
subject in writing that the Bank is unable to do so and give the reasons. The content 
of the letter must be reviewed by the Compliance Officer, Legal Department, 
Compliance Department and Corporate Communications Department before 
issued. The Bank must also fully comply with the request as soon as reasonably 
practicable after the expiry of the 40 day reply period. 
13.3. When filling out the form “Data Access Request Form (OPS003)” (Appendix 25), 
customers should clearly indicate the personal information requested to access, so 
as to help the Bank to handle it as soon as possible and avoid any disputes in future. 
Each unit should send a copy of the form to the Compliance Department so that the 
Compliance Department can monitor whether the Bank has responded within 40 
days after receiving the form. 
13.4. If the document requested by the customer involved third party personal 
information or internal approval, the handling staff must cover or delete such 
irrelevant information when copying the document or transaction record. If the 
customer has a joint/partnership/corporate account and the account information or 
document requested by the customer’s authorized signatory involved the personal 
information 
of 
other 
joint 
account 
holders/partners/company 
directors/shareholders, the Bank should ensure that the joint account 
holders/partners/directors/shareholders of the company sign together on the Data 
Access Request Form or the Photocopy of Documents Request Form (Appendix 
26) or the Bank has obtained their written consent in other ways before providing 
relevant information or document; if consent could not be obtained, the handling 
staff must cover or delete the personal information of the joint account 
holder/partner/company director/shareholder from relevant information or 
document. 
13.5. The copy of personal data to be supplied must be such personal data as is held at 
the time when the request is made. 
13.6. The Bank will be entitled to impose a reasonable, but not excessive charge with 
respect to a data access request. If a data subject or relevant person making a data 
access request asks for an additional copy of the personal data, the Bank may 
charge a fee to cover the full administrative and other costs in supplying such an 
=== PAGE 52 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 52 / 76 
additional copy. 
The information available for customers to access is divided into the following 
two categories:  
- Customer's personal data: Customers must fill in the “Data Access Request Form 
(OPS003)” (Appendix 25) (applicable to individual customers only) formulated 
by the Privacy Commissioner and the “Payment Form for Customer Personal 
Access Data (PDPO001)” (Appendix 27) to acknowledge the charges. 
13.6.1. - For copies of various account documents or transaction records/ details, 
etc.: The handling staff must first confirm the customer's identity and ask 
them to sign the “Photocopy of Document(s) Request Form (PDPO003)” 
(Appendix 26), and relevant fees will be levied from customers according 
to the relevant items in the Bank’s Service Charges.  
13.6.2. The Bank shall refuse to comply with a data access request under any of the 
following circumstances: 
13.6.3. if the Bank is not provided with sufficient information from a data subject 
or a relevant person on behalf of a data subject to identify the data subject; 
13.6.4. if the Bank is not provided with sufficient information to identify the person 
seeking the data, or not satisfied that the person seeking the data is properly 
authorized to do so; or 
13.6.5. if the personal data sought under the data access request comprises personal 
data of another individual and the Bank cannot comply with the request 
with disclosing the personal data of that other individual (unless the other 
individual has consented to such disclosure or the request can be complied 
with without disclosing the identity of that other individual). 
13.7. The Bank may refuse to comply with a data access request if : 
13.7.1. the request is not in writing in Chinese or English; 
13.7.2. the Bank is not provided with sufficient information to locate the personal 
data that are being requested; 
=== PAGE 53 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 53 / 76 
13.7.3. the request follows 2 or more similar request made by the data subject or a 
relevant person on his or her behalf and it is unreasonable for the Bank to 
comply; 
13.7.4. another data user controls the use of the personal data concerned in such a 
way that prohibits the Banks receiving the data access request form 
complying with the request; 
13.7.5. the data access request is not made in a form which has been specified under 
section 67 of the Ordinance; 
13.7.6. there is an applicable exemption from subject access provided for in Part 
VIII of the Ordinance; or 
13.7.7. the individual making a data access request has not paid any fee that is

13.8. The Compliance Department shall maintain a log book of all matters relating to

{"output": "15. Security of personal data and duty of confidentiality 
15.1. All personal data must be kept on secure files or computer retrieval systems to 
which access should only be granted to employees on a need-to-know basis.  
15.1.1. The warehouse gate should be closed at all times, and authorized personnel 
should hold the key and password to prevent unauthorized persons from 
entering and reading customer information without authorization. 
15.1.2. After office hours, all customer information must be properly kept, and the 
storage warehouse, audio records or cabinet where the information is stored 
must be locked.  
15.1.3. Various customer documents should be put in separate files for proper 
safekeeping.  
15.1.4. When sending documents containing personal information, envelopes, 
briefcases or folders must be used, and acknowledgement of receipt must 
be established as appropriate. If sent to customers via email, the file must 
be encrypted before sent.  
15.1.5. Customer information that is no longer used must be destroyed using a 
paper shredder, and the back of the paper with customer information printed 
on it should not be used for other purposes. 
15.1.6. When providing services to customers, in order to avoid leaking customer’s 
personal information to others, the Bank should:  
15.1.7. Place customer documents or information in appropriate locations.  
15.1.8. If the Bank staff only use the counter to communicate due to environmental 
constraints, the staff should try to reduce the volume.  
=== PAGE 57 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 57 / 76 
15.1.9. The employee’s access right to use the relevant computer system must be 
terminated immediately from the effective date of resignation or transfer.  
15.1.10. Any authorized auditor or government official who needs to access 
customer document for work must be requested to return the document on 
the same day.  
15.1.11. If a personal computer is used to store customer information, the relevant 
information must be properly kept.  
15.1.12. After using the computer to check customer information (FCR), the staff 
should leave the system (Sign Off) immediately.  
15.1.13. Personal passwords/access cards, etc. used to access the computer system 
should be carefully preserved and must not disclose to any person, 
including other current employees.  
15.1.14. Unless necessary for work, staff are not allowed to access customers’ 
personal information without authorization. 
15.1.15. Customer information should be stored in a locked storage or cabinet 
before leaving the workstation. 
15.1.16. The unit supervisors must regularly review whether the authorized staff 
need to access customer personal information in their work. Otherwise, they 
should notify the Information Technology Department to cancel the 
relevant authorization.  
15.1.17. The head of the unit must notify the Information Technology Department 
in advance of a list of transferred personnel (whose authorization is revoked) 
and their effective date, so that their authority to use the relevant computer 
systems will be terminated immediately on the effective date. 
15.1.18. When requested by other units to provide customer personal information, 
if colleagues have any doubts, colleagues should first check with the 
supervisor of the unit and consider whether to implement the relevant 
request based on the actual situation. 
=== PAGE 58 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 58 / 76 
15.2. Employees of the Bank must ensure that when dealing with a customer either in 
meeting or correspondence, that they do not negligently or indiscriminately 
disclose the customer’s personal data to unauthorized third parties. In particular, all 
correspondence sent (letters, facsimiles or emails) must be dispatched by the most 
secure method and/or in accordance with any prior instructions given by the 
customer. 
15.3. The Bank recognizes that it owes a general duty of confidentiality to its customers 
subject to three expectations: 
15.3.1. Where the Bank is required to disclose information under compulsion of 
law; 
15.3.2. Where the Bank discloses information with the express consent of a 
customer; and 
15.3.3. Where the disclosure is in the public interest. 
16. Accuracy and duration of retention of personal data 
16.1. The Bank should ensure accuracy of all personal data collected and processed by 
the Bank. Appropriate procedures should be implemented by individual unit to 
provide for all personal data to be checked and updated in the Bank’s records to 
ensure that it is reasonably accurate having regard to the purposes for which the 
data is or is to be used. 
16.2. In so far as personal data held by the Bank consists of statements of opinion, all 
reasonably practicable steps should be taken by the relevant unit to ensure that any 
facts cited in support of such statements of opinion are correct. 
16.3. If the handling staff uses customer information and doubts its accuracy (or is out 
of date), they must verify with the customer as soon as possible and obtain the latest 
information for updating. 
16.4. Regarding the retention period of telephone recordings and closed-circuit 
television tapes for surveillance records, please follow the Privacy Commissioner’s 
=== PAGE 59 ===
INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Compliance Department, Legal & Compliance Division 
Revised in January 2025 
        Page 59 / 76 
Guideline on Employee Monitoring and Personal Data Privacy at Work.  
16.5. Anonymized information should not be retained. Anonymization refers to the 
removal of identifiable elements from personal data so that it is no longer 
practicable to identify the individual directly or indirectly from the data. 
16.6. Personal data of customers or non-customers (such as outdated IC copy signed by 
authorized person or unapproved loan application document) which exceed data 
retention period should follow the data retention period to erase the data, no matter 
physical or digital form. The relevant erasure details e.g. when, by whom, and by 
what method, should be recorded in the “Personal Data Erasure Logsheet” 
(Appendix 24).

16.7. For various customer documents and audio recordings, please refer to paragraph 
1.1.3 above. 
17. Handling of personal data breach 
17.1. 
According to the “Guidance on Data Breach Handling and Data Breach 
Notifications” of the Privacy Commissioner (Appendix 32) , in case of personal data is 
exposed to the risk of loss, unauthorized or accidental access, processing, erasure or use, 
the Bank shall take active remedial steps to lessen the harm or damage. The Information 
Security Manager shall manage and handle the incident, coordinate with the PDCO, the 
Chief Risk Officer and other relevant functional units to take actions as follows: 
17.1.1. immediately gather the essential information relating to the incident; 
17.1.2. adopt appropriate measures to contain the risk exposure and impact;

{"output": "# 新规和版本变化 有新规、旧规替代、过渡期或用户要求判断会影响哪些内部控制时读本页。按[审查对象、规则效力与适用性](applicability.md)分别确认每地和每份制度的适用范围。 ## 先核哪套版本在何时适用 核对正式来源及修订关系。分别记发布日期、生效日、内部批准或发布日期、旧规停用日和过渡期截止，说明在审查基准日适用哪一版。现行与未来生效规则分别登记；未来生效事项可提前设计、培训和准备系统，但不得在实施日前默认改变客户体验或拒绝交易。旧版与新版并存时，按主体、场景和时间检查是否正常分段执行，明确旧控制停止日期。需要判断历史补录、补报、重核、迁移或补救时，从过渡、溯及条款或正式澄清查具体范围。新业务、存量关系、在途交易和持续义务分别判断；持续关系、资料过期或持续尽调触发可能要求重新评估。“不追溯”结论须由法律意见或监管书面确认支撑，不能只写“不适用”。 ## 按变化查影响位置 | 外规变化 | 重点查的内部落点 | | --- | --- | | 新增义务 | 主制度与本地细则、流程触发、岗位权限、表单、系统以及留痕。 | | 删除、替代或澄清义务 | 哪些旧规则失去原依据、哪些仍有其他适用依据，以及执行动作是否实质变化。 | | 定义、主体或对象变化 | 客户、账户、交易或数据范围，核术语、字段、分类、进入和退出流程，以及下游用到该分类的控制。 | | 阈值、期限或公式变化 | 口径、起算和临界值，核系统参数、取数或计算方式、审批例外、报表和历史重算。 | | 责任、权限或流程顺序变化 | 授权矩阵、职责承接、独立复核、系统权限、模板和培训。 | | 报送、留存或传输变化 | 报送字段、数据来源、时限、审批、报表生成和更正。另查归档、备份、日志、权限、供应商与跨境路径。 | | 原则或抽象标准变化 | 用官方解释确定动作、触发、例外和记录，再查现行做法能否达到要求。 | 基于现有材料判断是保持现有控制、澄清执行、修改制度还是联动流程、表单、系统、权限、合同、培训或报送。说明哪项适用、哪项仍待核。涉及实施、测试和责任安排时查[整改设计与验证](remediation.md)。 # 整改设计与验证 提出整改建议时选读相关段落。客户进入正式整改或要求验收方案时，再展开版本切换、批准和验收安排。 ## 建议落到具体动作 从已证实的差异出发，写清：原义务和控制目标、负责变更的制度或控制、要改的动作、整改后如何证明达标。政策原则、流程节点、字段、系统参数、授权矩阵、培训、合同和报送各改其实际受影响部分。将适用义务要求的改动、机构可选的增强和待确认的安排分别表述。根据证据说明影响新客户、存量关系、在途交易、数据、供应商或外部报告的范围。 ## 把责任绑定到控制 每项差异在工作记录中指定责任角色、截止日、验收证据、不确定性和人工复核人。按控制环节区分**负责人**、**执行人**、**复核或验证人**：正式整改的每个控制工件只有一个最终负责者；执行人可多个，但须按字段、模板、系统模块等具体工件拆分；复核人检查权限、结果或例外。正式整改可按客户已有管理框架补充批准、征询和知会角色。材料未证明岗位名称、授权或时限时写出待确认的角色和时点，法定时限另按适用依据记录，不虚构。 ## 形成正式变更包和批准链 正式整改建立变更包编号，至少归集：适用性结论及依据、制度旧版与新版、修订前后对照、法规原文及条款映射、术语和字段映射、批准记录、版本生效日、流程 SOP、模板、系统配置前后截图或工单、权限变更、培训材料、测试证据、例外审批、风险接受、回退方案、旧版撤回和只读归档位置。版本批准日、发布日、施行日和停用日分别记录；必要时按客户流程使用电子签、哈希校验和只读归档防止无痕替换。 按客户授权链完成业务真实性、监管要求、法律风险、数据保护或信息安全、系统可行性、风险接受和制度批准；需要管理层或董事会审批的按授权执行，不由分析者代批。剩余风险须记录评价、接受人、接受依据和后续监督，不能以修改文本代替风险关闭。 ## 准备证据和验收 - **验证控制变更。** 按场景选择应触发、不应触发、边界和人工例外，给出预期结果。看制度、流程、表单、系统字段或规则、权限、审批日志、报送和异常纠正记录是否一致。根据业务选择代表性样本，记下测试范围、偏差和复测结果。测试缺陷按阻断、重大、一般分级；正式变更由独立验证人员复核关键缺陷，阻断缺陷未关闭不得上线，关键缺陷须复测样本。 - **验证切换和补救。** 有版本变化时核生效、旧版撤回、双轨运行、历史补救、客户沟通与必要的回退准备。临时或补偿控制需明确负责人、批准、有效期、复核、证据与退出。按控制场景评价仍存在的风险。 - **按客户流程关闭。** 需要正式验收时应有批准记录、变更和发布版本、系统或权限工单、测试与必要复测、培训或通知、例外审批和后续监督记录。分别取得制度已批准、流程已修改、系统或参数已更新、人员已培训、新旧版本切换完成、历史业务补救或豁免的证明。分开报告已改文本、已上线、已验证及已关闭，任一必要环节缺证不标为已关闭。业务、合规、法务、信息科技、风险和审计的具体职责由客户流程确定。 - **回写并维护映射。** 整改关闭后更新法规状态、外部条款版本、控制矩阵、内部条款映射、差异台账、旧条款失效表、系统参数影响、培训影响、审计测试程序和整改关闭证据，保证后续正反查使用最新关系。 材料只支持制度审查时，可给出针对问题的改法和建议验收证据，继续交付已确认发现。 # 模糊条款的解释与可执行化 按本次涉及的主题选读。业务原件保留了所举监管文件、事件、案例和内部化建议的上下文。进入风险结论前，回到审查范围内现行且适用的原文，核对本机构的牌照、业务和控制证据。[业务原件](模糊条款的权威解释与可执行化_修订版.docx) ## 把原则转成可对照的要求 1. **先定位。** 从原则词及其定义、同义词、触发业务和后果找条款，再找适用版本的官方解释、指引、问答或个案。记录各自对应的条号、范围和适用时点。个案帮助识别风险场景和证据缺口。若资料中提到「本行」或某家分行，核对本次审查的法人或分行及其实际业务后再用。 2. **拆执行要求。** 写清哪个主体在什么条件下，由谁采取什么动作，何时完成，如何处理例外、升级与复核，留下什么证据。监管原文规定的时限、阈值和口径照原文写。机构自行设定的频率、预警阈值或服务时限按内部标准核对。 3. **找承接证据。** 先看制度主条款，再找操作手册、授权、表单、系统参数、结果记录或报送底稿。对照正常、例外和边界情形，看现有控制是否达到同一目标。缺少固定数字或用语不同本身不足以判定风险，需指出哪个执行要素不足、什么场景会受影响。 4. **分开落结论。** 已确认适用义务与现有控制有实质差异的，写明原文及位置、解释依据的作用、控制缺陷和整改动作。只有解释或案例线索时可记录待核项或建议性增强。若原文只定原则，重点核内规是否给出可执行、可监督的安排，定级按已证实的差异和影响。 ## {"content":"# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""PDP 内规：整项缺失类制度级缺口"""
import json, os

OUT = "/home/agent/.hermes/profiles/aito/workspaces/user-803/work/findings"
ALT = "Consumer Protection in the Use of Alternat.pdf"
IC6 = "IC-6.PDF"
CLOUD = "Practice guide on cloud adoption.pdf"

recs = []

recs.append({"区域": "制度级缺口", "风险等级": "高", "差异类型": "漏洞",
 "外规文件名": IC6,
 "外规条款号": "7.3 / 7.4",
 "外规正文":
 "7.3 In particular, all retail banks (including digital banks) are required to engage more than one CRA to ensure operational resilience and continuity of consumer credit services. "
 "These banks are expected to be able to switch over swiftly and seamlessly between CRAs to maintain full credit risk assessment capabilities and consumer credit services, covering key services such as credit reports, data correction, and related credit risk management functions. "
 "In the event of service disruption of a CRA, these banks are expected to complete the switch-over and resume normal business operations within 24 hours without any degradation in consumer credit services and in risk management and control. "
 "All retail banks (including digital banks) are required to conduct drills at least once every 12 months, covering technical, operational, and risk management aspects, to demonstrate their ability to migrate seamlessly between CRAs. "
 "Following each drill, all retail banks are expected to obtain written confirmation from their non-primary CRA(s), verifying the successful completion of all activities and the attainment of key operational objectives. "
 "These banks should have clear policy and procedures setting out the above, as well as effective controls and monitoring functions in place to ensure that they are capable of conducting the switch-over. Such policy and procedures should be subject to review of the banks’ management.\n\n"
 "7.4 Any AI engaging a CRA shall ensure that all consumer credit data is collected, stored, and processed by the CRA and the operator of the Credit Reference Platform within Hong Kong for effective oversight and consumer protection. "
 "No transfer of consumer credit data outside Hong Kong shall be permitted except for genuine credit applications outside Hong Kong initiated and expressly authorised by the consumer, such as under the Cross-Boundary Credit Referencing initiative. "
 "Transfers solely for technical or operational convenience, even with customer consent, are not permitted, as they would undermine the integrity of the CDS and expose consumers to risks outside of Hong Kong’s regulatory framework. "
 "AIs shall monitor compliance with this clause through contractual obligations, audit rights, and regular reporting from the CRA and the operator of the Credit Reference Platform.",
 "缺失分析":
 "【适用性】IC-6 V.7（2026年6月12日）为金管局依《银行业条例》第16(10)条发出的法定指引，适用对象为从事消费信贷的认可机构。本行为香港认可机构零售银行，实际开展消费信贷及按揭业务，第7.3条（须聘用多于一家CRA、24小时内切换、每12个月至少一次切换演练并取得非主要CRA书面确认）与第7.4条（消费信贷资料须由CRA及信贷资料平台营办商在香港境内收集、储存与处理，除境外真实信贷申请并经客户明确授权外不得转移出境）均直接适用。上海分行不属本指引适用对象，故本项只针对香港总行。\n\n"
 "【承接依据】本行《客户个人资料保护指引》第11段为CRA资料共享与使用的专门章节，第11.1条明确“the departments involving in the sharing or use of personal data through CRAs should act in line with the requirements stipulated in… Supervisory Policy Manual IC-6”，即本段承担承接IC-6的义务，第11段是本制度审查下该义务的主承接位置。\n\n"
 "【已查文件与版本】《Guidelines on Personal Data Protection for Customers》（2025年1月23日修订，76页全文含第1–20段、附录1–34）、《CRS Guideline》（2026年8月27日修订）、《Guideline on Mainland China and Taiwan Business Activities》（2025年8月13日修订）、《IC-6》V.7（2026年6月12日）、《Practice Guide on Cloud Adoption》（2026年1月）、《Consumer Protection in the Use of Alternative Data》（2026年3月26日）、PCPD新闻稿（2024年8月22日）。\n\n"
 "【六维检索范围】以“CRA / credit reference agency / Credit Data Smart / CDS / MCRA / 信贷资料平台 / 信用资料服务机构 / switch-over / 切换 / resilience / 演练 / drill / 香港境内储存 / data residency / cross-boundary credit referencing”为中英文关键词，在PDP指引全文（含附录清单与版本控制表）、CRS指引、内地及台湾业务活动指引中检索：PDP指引第11.1–11.2.2及附录16仅列示可提供资料范围与须遵守的准则名称；CRS指引全文无CRA或信贷资料平台条款；内地及台湾业务活动指引不涉及；未在任何已查文件中找到“聘用多于一家CRA”“切换演练”“非主要CRA书面确认”“消费信贷资料不得转移出境”的对应控制。\n\n"
 "【最接近的控制及其不能覆盖的理由】最接近的是第11.1条对IC-6的整体引用——该条只是声明须遵守IC-6，并未就第7.3、7.4条设定本行的具体动作（聘用家数、切换时限、演练频率、书面确认的取得与留存、离岸转移的禁止与例外审批）。此外第9段外判与第8A/8B段跨境转移针对的是“个人资料”的一般跨境规则，允许在取得同意或采用适当保障后跨境；而IC-6第7.4条对消费信贷资料设置了更严格的属地要求（仅限境外真实信贷申请并经明确授权，技术或运营便利目的即使客户同意亦不允许），两者标准不同、不能互相替代。故认定为本行应承接而全文、附件及引用文件均无对应控制，构成制度级缺口（漏洞）。\n\n"
 "【待核】IC-6第7.3条针对“retail banks”，本行的零售银行资格与CRA聘用现状（是否已聘用CRS/CDS下多于一家CRA、切换演练记录、非主要CRA的书面确认）未在本批材料中提供，需业务单位补充确认后据以判断执行层面是否已达标；第7.4条的合约条款与CRA定期报告若已在下层外包或供应商管理文件中规定，需取得该等文件以更新本项归属。"})

"""把 F(...)/G(...) 调用内“相邻字符串缺少逗号”的形式统一改成显式 + 拼接。"""
import re, sys

inside = False

    s = l.lstrip()
    if re.match(r"^[FG]\(", s):
        inside = True
        out.append(l)
        continue
    if inside and s.startswith('"'):
        # string literal line: if previous line inside call ended with a string literal
        # (i.e. ended with `"` or `\n"`), it needs an explicit +
        prev = out[-1].rstrip() if out else ""
        if prev and not prev.endswith(",") and not prev.endswith("(") and not prev.endswith("+"):
            indent = l[: len(l) - len(s)]
            l = indent + "+ " + s

    if inside and s.startswith(")"):
        inside = False
        out.append(l)
        continue
    if inside and (s.startswith("+ ") or s.startswith('+ ')):
        out.append(l)
        continue
    # leave everything else untouched
    inside = inside and not s.startswith(")")
    out.append(l)

open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out))

"""Fix missing `+` between string/token lines inside F(...)/G(...) calls.

A line needs a leading `+` when the previous non-empty line inside the call does
not already end with an operator (`,`, `(`, `+`).
"""
import re, sys

path = sys.argv[1]
src = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
out = []
inside = False
for raw in src:
    s = raw.strip()
    if not inside:
        if re.match(r"^[FG]\(", s):
            inside = True
        out.append(raw)
        continue
    if s.startswith(")"):
        inside = False
        out.append(raw)
        continue
    prev = out[-1].rstrip() if out else ""
    ends_open = (not prev) or prev.endswith(",") or prev.endswith("(") or prev.endswith("+")
    if not ends_open:
        indent = raw[: len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip())]
        raw = indent + "+ " + raw.lstrip()
    out.append(raw)

open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out))
print("rewritten", path)","path":"/home/agent/.hermes/profiles/aito/workspaces/user-803/work/fixplus.py"}

## 审查结论

共 **21 条**问题：条款差异 16 条、制度级缺口 5 条；风险等级高 9 条、中 9 条、低 3 条。问题类型：差距 15 条、漏洞 5 条、责任缺口 1 条。

| 内规 | 条目 | 高 | 中 | 低 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guidelines on PDP for Customers（2025-01-23） | 11 | 3 | 5 | 3 |
| CRS Guideline（2026-08-27） | 5 | 3 | 2 | 0 |
| Mainland China and Taiwan Business Activities（2025-08-13） | 5 | 3 | 2 | 0 |

**最需要优先处理的五项（高风险且属制度级漏洞）**：

1. **IC-6 V.7 第 7.3/7.4 条未被承接**：未规定聘用多于一家 CRA、24 小时内切换、每 12 个月一次切换演练并取得非主要 CRA 书面确认；也未规定消费信贷资料须在香港境内处理，且除境外真实信贷申请外禁止出境（该条比一般个人资料跨境规则更严，不能以取得客户同意替代）。
2. **云端服务提供者（CSP）的合同最低条款、退出策略、云事故管理与云监控整项缺失**：内规第 9 段只对“Service Provider”作了原则性要求，未区分 IaaS/PaaS/SaaS 三种服务模式。
3. **CRS 合理性测试只有“须做”，没有任何“怎么做”**：未列出比对要素，也未指定执行人、复核层级、不通过处理和记录格式。
4. **CRS 记录保存只规定“存 7 年”，未规定可检索性、保存介质、访问控制、销毁审批与销毁证据**，无法满足“随时可核验申报准确性”。
5. **内地及台湾业务指引只管控“职员出访”，未管控远程渠道与系统/数据所在地**，无法判断向当地客户提供远程服务是否触发当地牌照或数据本地化要求。

此外还有三项高风险条款差距值得关注：CRA 报告存取控制（授权、季度更换密码、日志字段、异常比对、销毁）；客户资料查阅日志与异常监测（“谁在何时为何看了谁的资料”无法证明）；外访法律意见没有更新频率，也未界定“业务活动”是否包含线上和转介。

## 需要你确认或补充的事项

- **下层文件未提供**：资讯保安管理指引、外包政策及指引、CRS 操作规程/FATCA-CRS 操作手册、云采用政策、记录保存政策、Cross-border Business Activities database。若这些文件已有对应控制，相关条目应改归“条款差异”而非“制度级缺口”。这是目前影响归类的最主要变量。
- **运行证据**：CRA 聘用家数与切换演练记录、云端资产与外包功能登记册、CRS 合理性测试覆盖率、客户资料查阅日志样本。
- **分工确认**：三份内规均把适用范围延伸到内地分行，但上海分行的本地对应义务（内地征信办法、PIPL、非居民金融账户尽调办法）需另行取得分行本地指引，才能判断集团与分行之间的承接是否衔接。
- **PCPD 新版身份证指引正文**只在材料中提供了新闻稿，具体条款需取得《资料使用者指引》原文后复核（已在该条待核中列明）。

审查方法按 skill 执行：逐条正查＋逐项反查、四层适用性筛选（主体/牌照业务/场景/属地外溢）、差异类型与风险等级分别判断；每条记录均标注了内规原文位置与外规条款出处。
